newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU exclusion deal report absurd - French official.
newsitem.headline: EMU exclusion deal report absurd - French official.

text.p: A French finance ministry official said on Wednesday a newspaper report that Bonn and Paris were preparing a deal to exclude Italy and Spain from the start of European monetary union was completely absurd.
"It's totally absurd," the official said when asked to comment on a report in Italy's Il Sole 24 Ore, which said a deal was taking shape between the German and French governments.

The Milan newspaper said in an article by its Frankfurt correspondent quoting "sources in Bonn": "thanks to the threat, still latent, of a two-year delay in the euro (single currency), Bonn has managed in the last three weeks to convince Paris of the importance that Germany attaches to the temporary exclusion of Italy from the first group of single currency countries".
"But since it is considered politically too risky to abandon Italy as the only excluded one together with Greece, (the idea of) similar treatment for Spain is gaining ground," it said.

Similar reports of deals to delay Italian entry have emerged in the past several months, with one British newspaper story on the issue in February provoking a chorus of denials from the governments of Germany, Italy and France as well as the European Commission.
